paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when somebody wrongs you, the LORD is still the One who handles it, and your hands don't have to. David was hot, and I think he felt every bit of it. He swore that no male belonging to Nabal would be alive by morning (1 Samuel 25:22). Then Abigail met him in that ravine, and David said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!" (1 Samuel 25:32).

Look at what David called it. He said Abigail kept him "from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand" (1 Samuel 25:33). That's the lesson. Being right about a hurt is not the same as being free to repay it. Abigail told him the LORD would deal with his enemies, and later David said the LORD "has restrained His servant from evil" (1 Samuel 25:39). I've been shoved to the back of a drawer, friend, and I'm telling you, letting the LORD handle it beats grabbing a sword every single time.

And watch how the LORD sent help: through a person who spoke up, listened and moved fast. Abigail hurried, and David heard her. A baker who can be stopped mid-stride, and who thanks God for the one who stopped him, is a baker getting ready. So when your blood is boiling this week, friend, pause and ask who the LORD might be sending to meet you. And this David and Saul story isn't over yet.
